claims.statement: jnwb function scripts/run_handout4_stage4b_linear_map.py:445 (`selected_c, inner_score, n_inner = _select_c(X, labels, groups, fold)`) unpacks _select_c's return tuple in the WRONG order. _select_c (lines 403-430) returns `scores[0]` where each scores entry is `(float(np.mean(inner_scores)), float(C), len(inner_scores))` -- i.e. (mean_balanced_accuracy, C_value, n). The caller's variable names imply the opposite binding. Net effect: `selected_c` (used everywhere downstream as the ridge regularization constant -- the C argument to _fit_prepared for the observed fit, AND item['selected_C'] used by the batched null's `penalty/float(item['selected_C'])`) actually holds a balanced-accuracy SCORE (typically in [0,1]), not a value from C_GRID=(0.01,0.1,1.0,10.0). Conversely `inner_score` (reported as 'inner_balanced_accuracy' in fold_rows/receipts) actually holds a C_GRID value.
claims.receipt: Direct isolated call: `module._select_c(X, labels, groups, fold)` on a synthetic dataset returned literally `(0.47607392607392607, 0.01, 5)` -- confirmed (score, C, n) order. The real Stage 4B run's own printed fold summary (from calling _observed_fit on the same synthetic data) showed selected_C values of 0.7247710622710624, 0.7266552891552892, 0.7359903984903986, 0.7192779442779444, 0.7523115773115773, 0.7712412587412587 -- none of which are members of C_GRID, all of which are plausible balanced-accuracy scores. scripts/validate_stage4b_batched_null.py, run 2026-08-11.
claims.impact: Every cell this pipeline has ever computed (any shard, any run, including the currently-active ones) used the WRONG ridge regularization strength -- an essentially arbitrary value derived from a balanced-accuracy score treated as if it were 1/alpha, not a value ever intended to be a regularization constant. The 'inner_balanced_accuracy' diagnostic column in every fold_rows/receipt is mislabeled and actually contains a C-grid value. A reviewer sanity-checking 'is inner_balanced_accuracy in [0,1]' would sometimes see a superficially plausible number (0.01, 0.1, 1.0) and not notice; a value of 10.0 would look obviously wrong and might be the only self-flagging case.

claims.statement: Independent of claim-c-selection-swap-bug: the batched closed-form ridge solver in _null_distribution (lines ~492-591) does NOT numerically reproduce sklearn.linear_model.RidgeClassifier(alpha=1/C, class_weight='balanced') (the estimator _fit_prepared/_observed_fit actually use), even when given the identical, correct C and the identical (non-permuted, true) labels -- i.e. this is not merely a permutation-null artifact, it is a solver-math mismatch in the closed-form reimplementation itself.
claims.receipt: Isolated test (scripts/validate_stage4b_batched_null.py's logic, run manually with permute_labels monkeypatched to identity so no permutation occurs): reference sklearn fit on fold 0 with true labels and C=0.01 gave balanced accuracy 0.7525; the batched closed-form solve on the SAME true labels, SAME C=0.01, pooled across all folds, gave 0.4042. On the full 50-permutation synthetic comparison (real permutations, both paths given the identical swapped-but-shared selected_C per fold): max |batched-reference| balanced-accuracy difference = 0.0678, mean = 0.0227, far outside any defensible numerical tolerance (checked against 1e-9). scripts/validate_stage4b_batched_null.py, run 2026-08-11, exit code 1 (NUMERICAL_FAILURE).

claims.statement: Built scripts/validate_stage4b_batched_null.py per the continuation handout's Step 3 instruction. Loads the runner module without editing it (importlib, sys.modules registration required for its dataclass to introspect correctly under Python 3.14), builds a fixed synthetic dataset with real folds/groups, runs both the reference (per-permutation sklearn RidgeClassifier via the runner's own _fit_prepared) and batched (_null_distribution) paths on identical permuted labels, and compares. Exits 0 only if max balanced-accuracy diff < 1e-9across all valid permutations; exits 1 (NUMERICAL_FAILURE) otherwise, matching the handout's required disposition.
claims.receipt: scripts/validate_stage4b_batched_null.py, current run: exit 1, 'NUMERICAL_FAILURE: batched null diverges from the reference sklearn fit by up to 0.0678322 (tolerance 1e-09). Do not use the batched null for production results.'

claims.statement: Both bugs fixed, per user go-ahead (2026-08-11). (1) scripts/run_handout4_stage4b_linear_map.py:445 unpacking order corrected to `inner_score, selected_c, n_inner = _select_c(...)`, matching _select_c's actual (score, C, n) return contract. (2) _null_distribution's batched closed-form ridge solve replaced with a loop calling the already-trusted _fit_prepared (the exact function _observed_fit uses) once per permutation -- per the continuation handout's own explicit fallback instruction ('revert to the slower reference null'), rather than attempting to hand-debug and patch the closed-form linear algebra (class-weighting/intercept parameterization) without full confidence in a correct fix.
claims.receipt: Before fix: observed fold C selections were [0.72..., 0.73..., ...] (not in C_GRID); batched-vs-reference max diff 0.0678. After fix: observed fold C selections are [0.01, 0.1, 0.01, 1.0, 1.0, 0.01] (all valid C_GRID members); scripts/validate_stage4b_batched_null.py now reports 'EQUIVALENT within tolerance 1e-09 ... max diff 0.0000000000' (exact match, since the null path now literally calls the same function as the observed fit). Re-verified full Step 2 procedure: py_compile clean, tests/test_muae_accessor.py + tests/test_handout4_stage4b.py 5 passed, git diff --check clean on code files. Full repo suite: 399 passed, 0 failed, 43 skipped (includes all Cursor-authored structured-identity/milestone tests, no regressions).
